quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What can cause motorcycle collisions?
questions.explanation: Following too closely behind another vehicle causes many motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent attention than cars. Check your motorcycle for problems before riding. It is critical to find any issues before riding in traffic or on highways.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway right away.
Practice with it in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice riding it in a safe, controlled area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left part of the lane, next to the center line.
The right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes depending on the situation. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space around you. Move to a different position as traffic changes.

questions.question: What footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection when riding. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to a single line when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: You should keep a greater distance between you and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: If the road surface is slippery.
If you can see through the vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road surface is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. If the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy, maintain at least a four-second following distance.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket, a motorcycle rider should look for one that is:

options.text: Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear a protective jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly but allows free movement. Leather or sturdy synthetic material with body armor offers the best protection.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather or sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: If you have one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your riding skills. Any amount of alcohol is not safe before riding.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes when you stop.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car crashes happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you are most comfortable.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: The left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This position helps you avoid doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Be ready to change your position as conditions change.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are never very strong.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter medications, have side effects that can impair your riding ability. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over bridge gratings. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get over the surface faster.
Maintain a steady speed and ride straight across the gratings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed and ride straight across the gratings.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight. Do not try to zigzag to stay in your lane.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a passenger vehicle's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a larger vehicle's brake light. Other drivers may not see your brake light, especially when your taillight is on.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: Where is the biggest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The biggest risk is at intersections. The main danger is oncoming cars turning left in front of motorcycles.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcyclist most visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is best when following a car because it puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions change.

questions.question: How should you brake when making a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply both the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, keep going.

questions.question: Can motorcyclists use High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes?
questions.explanation: In Tennessee, motorcyclists can use HOV lanes anytime, no matter how many riders are on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What separates traffic lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean no passing. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal once you complete your turn or lane change. Leaving it on can confuse other drivers.

questions.question: What should motorcyclists do about the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: Find the lane with the least amount of oil.

questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can stay to the left or right side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.
